findings.source_passage: I didn't want to reveal any sort of escape plan I could devise, if my mind could devise one for me. At the moment, it was a little tired, and her suggestion of rest was a little too tempting.
findings.source_locator: After the escape-route speech, before 'Her shrunken hand settled on my shoulder'
findings.why_it_matters: This interiority — the narrator's wry self-deprecating aside about her own tired mind and the ironic admission that rest was tempting — is a small but characteristic register moment that reveals the narrator's voice. Its absence flattens the transition to the branding scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the parenthetical self-awareness: 'I didn't want to reveal any escape plan I could devise, if my mind could devise one — at the moment it was a little tired, and her suggestion was a little too tempting.'

findings.source_passage: I inspected the room for sources of escape… The drop was sixty feet to the packed ground… too far to jump, but not too far to climb down. The numerous sheets on the bed would be my rope. I went to work pulling and tying. In a half hour I had my rope.
findings.source_locator: After the lock clicks, before looking out the window for sentries
findings.why_it_matters: The source's crisp, declarative action sentences ('I went to work pulling and tying. In a half hour I had my rope.') carry a dry, matter-of-fact voice rhythm that is signature to the narrator's tone under pressure. The draft compresses this to 'I worked knots. In half an hour I had a length of linen,' losing both the pacing and the exact phrase 'my rope' which echoes the protagonist's ownership of her own plan.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the source's sentence rhythm: 'I went to work pulling and tying. In half an hour I had my rope.' The blunt finality of that short sentence is part of the narrator's voice.

findings.source_passage: The inmates were celebrating their torment of six women. I had to hurry lest this dragon lord show me off to his drunken friends.
findings.source_locator: After securing the rope to the bedstead, before slipping over the window frame
findings.why_it_matters: The word 'inmates' is a loaded, ironic character detail — the narrator frames her captors as the ones who are institutionalized — and 'their torment of six women' specifies solidarity with the other captives. The draft replaces this with vague 'celebrating' and 'drunken friends,' losing the ironic framing.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'inmates' and the phrase 'their torment of six women' to preserve the narrator's sardonic reframe of the power dynamic.

findings.source_passage: The grounds remained deserted. They all celebrated their triumph of us and talked their insane talk about rival dragon clans.
findings.why_it_matters: The source's closing line frames the chapter's end with 'their triumph of us' — a communal 'us' that ties the narrator back to the other captive women. The draft loses this solidarity note, ending instead on 'rival dragon clans while I slipped into the dark,' which is more cinematic but erases the thematic emphasis on collective captivity.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'their triumph of us' in the closing beat to preserve the chapter's thematic ending note.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; two medium-severity voice-flattening instances (the narrator's self-deprecating interiority mid-chapter and the rope-making action rhythm) and two low-severity losses (the 'inmates' ironic reframe and the closing 'us' solidarity note) — below the regeneration threshold but worth correcting in revision.
